subject: Support for a Strong Medford Tree Ordinance
overview: The committee finalized logistics for the upcoming Harvest Your Energy Festival and reviewed the progress of the city's new solid waste contract and zero-waste goals. Members also debated and ultimately approved a motion reaffirming their support for a comprehensive tree ordinance that covers both public and private property.

items.title: Quorum and Introductions
items.summary: The chair established a quorum and introduced guest representatives from the Tufts Energy Group and a city intern assisting with planning and engineering projects.

items.title: Approval of Minutes
items.summary: Approved the minutes from the September committee meeting.

items.title: Administrative Updates
items.summary: Alicia Hunt reported on the hiring of a new building commissioner, the reposting of the facilities manager position, and recent community outreach successes at the Mystic River Celebration.

items.title: Tufts Energy Group Update
items.summary: Rosemary Lohr discussed the group's involvement in an upcoming energy symposium and a presentation by Block Power regarding municipal funding for residential heat pump projects.

items.title: Harvest Your Energy Festival Planning
items.summary: Lauretta James detailed festival logistics, including the participation of 40 exhibitors and 13 sponsors, food truck arrangements, and musical performances.

items.title: Solid Waste Contract and Task Force Progress
items.summary: The committee reviewed the timeline for the city's new solid waste contract, which includes exploring zero-waste goals, RFID tracking for bins, and stricter state regulations regarding mattress and textile disposal.

items.title: Medford Tree Ordinance Discussion
items.summary: Members discussed a City Council decision to split the draft tree ordinance into three separate sections—public trees, private trees, and the tree committee—for further refinement and legal review.

items.title: Motion to Support Tree Ordinance
items.summary: Approved a motion to reaffirm the committee's general support for a strong tree ordinance covering both public and private trees following a debate over potential financial penalties for primary homeowners.
